rawFindings.title: Incorrect use of url.resolve for constructing asset path
rawFindings.explanation: The original code returns the asset path relative to the public directory by joining post.path and this.slug using path.join, which preserves the exact filename and path. The updated code replaces this with url.resolve(post.path, this.slug), which treats the input as URLs, potentially normalizing or resolving slashes in a way that changes the intended file path. rawFindings.title: Improper URL joining for 'path' virtual in PostAsset model
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces pathFn.join with url.resolve to join post.path and this.slug. pathFn.join joins filesystem paths and may not produce valid URLs when slugs contain spaces or special characters, but url.resolve resolves URLs according to URL rules, which differs in behavior and might produce unexpected results if post.path or this.slug are not absolute URLs. This change may cause incorrect URL paths being generated for PostAsset.path, potentially breaking asset URL resolution.
rawFindings.suggestion: Either revert to using pathFn.join as before (given the comment about no need to urlescape), or sanitize and encode URL components properly before resolving URLs. Ensure that the method used produces correct relative URLs as expected by the system.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect use of url.resolve for path joining in PostAsset.path virtual attribute
rawFindings.explanation: The diff changes PostAsset.path virtual getter to use url.resolve(post.path, this.slug) instead of path.join(post.path, this.slug). url.resolve is intended for URL resolution and normalizes slashes, treating the second argument as an absolute path if it starts with '/', which can lead to incorrect path resolution especially in a filesystem context or when post.path is not a full URL. This may break the expected behavior of forming the asset path relative to public_dir.
rawFindings.suggestion: Replace url.resolve(post.path, this.slug) with pathFn.join(post.path, this.slug) to correctly join filesystem paths and avoid unexpected URL normalization.
